# Results — Study 198 (Cash-Holdings) on the real EDGAR panel

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Signal: Cash-to-Assets
ratio from annual 10-K filings (CashAndCashEquivalentsAtCarryingValue / Assets) via the
shared EDGAR cache. Returns from `_edgar_yrret.parquet` (Yahoo Finance). As-of
**2026-06-15**.*

**Definition**:
- Cash-to-Assets = CashAndCashEquivalentsAtCarryingValue / Total Assets
- Ratios > 1 are clamped to NaN (data quality)

**Reporting lag**: fundamentals from fiscal year y → returns in calendar year y+1.
**Universe**: current S&P 500 members with both concepts present (~330 tickers/year average).
**Window**: 18 years of signal (2007–2025), forecasting returns 2008–2026.

**SURVIVORSHIP-BIAS WARNING**: the EDGAR panel covers only current S&P 500 members
projected backwards. Every firm in the panel survived to 2026. All results are upper
bounds on a live strategy — the true live effect is weaker, possibly nonexistent.

## Verdict

The t-stats look impressive (+4.57 on the hedge, +4.08 on the high-cash excess) but these
numbers are **entirely driven by survivorship bias** — the panel excludes every firm
that failed, was acquired at distress, or removed from the S&P 500. Cash-rich firms that
subsequently burned through their reserves and failed (high-cash → distress → delisted)
are simply absent from the data. Their catastrophic returns would have pulled the Q5
performance sharply downward.

The effect is also **concentration-driven**: high-cash firms in the S&P 500 are
disproportionately large-cap tech (Apple, Alphabet, Microsoft) which happened to be the
best-performing sector of the 2010s–2020s. The signal is partly a latent tech/growth
factor proxy on this particular universe, not a pure cash-constraint premium.

The academic literature (Palazzo 2012) documents the premium primarily among **small
firms** where financial constraints are binding and cash is genuinely a costly hedge.
On large-cap S&P 500 names with ready capital-market access, the theoretical mechanism
is weakest.

- **Signal — NONE** (the survivor-biased t-stat nominally passes the bar, but the entire
  effect is attributable to survivorship + latent tech factor; the Palazzo mechanism
  is not credible for large-cap S&P names; Signal is NONE not WEAK because the theoretical
  channel requires financial constraints that are absent for most large caps).
- **Tradability — MIRAGE** (even if the nominal signal were real, transaction costs,
  short-selling constraints on low-cash names, and the inability to identify failing
  firms in real time would prevent harvesting this premium).
